claim: `git update-index --split-index` empties the index of this repository. In a linked worktree with nothing else running it took 352,440 entries to none, and setting `core.splitIndex` on this checkout and leaving the next write to convert did the same to 352,306. Every timing that made a split index look cheap was taken after that emptying, against an index holding nothing, so none of them says what a split index costs. No commit was ever harmed: a landing builds its tree from the tree at HEAD rather than from the index. The one run that kept its entries was a `--shared` clone, and nothing says why that one differed.

evidence:
Measured on 2026-09-16 with git 2.55.0, against this repository, whose index holds about 352,400 entries in 58MiB.

On this checkout: `git config core.splitIndex true`, and the next index write left `.git/index` at 7.2MiB beside a 168-byte `sharedindex.0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`, with `git ls-files` answering nothing. `folder-matches-a-shape` then refused every folder it was handed, which is what a check reading an empty tree says, so every landing in those three minutes was refused. `git read-tree HEAD` put the index back at 352,427 entries with nothing staged, in 343ms, and the commits across the window were all ordinary.

In a linked worktree, with six processes staging paths and running `git status` in a loop, `git update-index --split-index` left the index at no entries within a second of running. In a second linked worktree with nothing else running at all, the same call took 352,440 entries to none. So neither concurrency nor the route explains it, and converting an index of this size is what fails.

That is also what the earlier timings were measuring. `--split-index` ran first and the index was timed after, so `stage one path 63ms to 14ms`, `git status 477ms to 9ms`, and three hundred stages at mean 14.4ms were all taken against an index holding nothing. They say what an empty index costs. The one number that holds is from a `--shared` clone of this repository, where akasha's own `committed` took 150.0ms and 146.4ms before the split and 76.1ms, 71.8ms and 72.0ms after it, with `git status --porcelain -uno` clean after each commit and `git fsck --connectivity-only` clean at the end. Why that clone converted and kept its entries is not established.

Index version 4 was measured on the same worktree before any split: the file went from 58MiB to 34MiB and a write went from 63ms to 65ms. Those two were taken against a whole index, and they say the cost is per-entry work rather than bytes, so shrinking the file buys nothing.
